event: On St. Brigid's second-floor hall, Nimue fills a coffee cup, six minutes left on her shift.

memory.fact: Nimue was near the end of a twelve-hour night shift when the System descended.
Nimue's shift had run long, and was in its sixth-to-last minute when the System descended.

event: She has mapped the hall without meaning to: two exits, the crash cart, the drunk in 210.

memory.fact: Nimue compulsively keeps a running tally of any space she is in.

event: Even off the clock she counts the room: who's breathing, what's between her and the door.

memory.fact: Nimue counts exits, threats, who's breathing, and what's between her and the door.
Nimue counts who's going to need her before this is over.
Nimue counts the room even off the clock.
Nimue's mother called it being unable to sit still in her own life.
Nimue calls counting the room doing her job.

event: Flat blue-white text hangs in the air before her: THE SYSTEM HAS DESCENDED.

memory.fact: The System descended over the city at about 4:51 AM.
The System announced: THE SYSTEM HAS DESCENDED.
The System announced: Assessment of local lifeforms is complete.
The System communicates in flat blue-white text at the exact focal distance of the viewer's eye.
The System's blue-white emits no light and casts no glow.
The System's font was never once written by a hand.

event: Coffee overflows the cup and scalds her fingers; she leaves them there.
The System: 99.4% fail the threshold for Ascension; culling completes in 00:60:00.

memory.fact: 99.4% of assessed lifeforms did not meet the threshold for Ascension.
After the assessment, a countdown began: culling will complete in 00:60:00.
The countdown said the unascended will be cleared.
The ascended are those who pass the System's assessment.
The unascended are those who fail the System's assessment and are culled.

event: A countdown starts in the corner of her eye, and she cannot blink it off.

memory.fact: The System's notifications are printed on the inside of the eye.
The culling countdown tracks with head movement and cannot be blinked away.

event: Down the hall Devon laughs, then drops mid-step without putting his hands out.

memory.fact: The unascended simply ceased to hold themselves up.

event: Nimue is over him at once: no pulse, no breath, no wound, pupils blown and fixed.

memory.fact: Those who failed the assessment died instantly at assessment, with no wound and no struggle.

event: She starts compressions anyway, elbows locked, counting.

memory.fact: Nimue is a 31-year-old trauma and ER nurse at St. Brigid's hospital.
Under crisis Nimue runs on algorithm: you do not feel anything until afterward, you just work.

event: Soft thuds sound through the whole hospital and the whole city as people drop.

memory.fact: The Fall, or First Cull, is the world-ending event at the System's descent.
Soft impacts sounded all over the hospital and the city: a species being switched off.

event: A footnote: resuscitation will not restore an unascended subject; nothing to repair.

memory.fact: Resuscitation cannot restore an unascended subject; it is not a wound, and nothing can be repaired.
The System is a non-human intelligence.
The System does not hate or gloat.
The System's notes are informative.
The System told Nimue, helpfully, that her CPR could not work.
The System hands over such notes the way it would hand over useful data.
The System measured Devon, found a number too low, and tidied him away without cruelty.

event: Nimue does six more compressions, then stops, because the System is right.

memory.fact: Nimue refuses to keep doing what doesn't work.
Nimue did CPR on a colleague, Devon, who dropped dead at the cull; it failed.

event: She stands, knees wet with spilled coffee, as the clock reads 00:57:12.
Priya from peds seizes her wrist and begs her to say what to do.

memory.fact: Priya is a pediatrics nurse at St. Brigid's.
Priya's night station is two doors from Nimue's.
Priya is ascended.
When the cull hit, Priya seized Nimue's wrist and begged for reassurance and a plan.
Priya begged Nimue: what is it, tell me what to do, please.

event: Nimue reaches in herself for warm reassurance and finds it is not there.

memory.fact: Priya wanted warm comfort.
When Priya begged Nimue for comfort, Nimue felt the warm reassurance absent in herself.
Nimue felt that absence the way you feel a tooth that should be there and isn't.

event: She grips Priya in a transport hold and orders her to the south stairwell, away from windows.

memory.fact: Nimue answered Priya with a clinical hand-squeeze, a transport-hold, and an order.
Nimue ordered Priya to the south stairwell, away from the windows, now.
Nimue's core flaw is self-reliance as a wall: hands, not heart.
Nimue offers competence and instruction in place of warmth.
Nimue goes home to an empty apartment and tells herself she prefers it.

event: Priya looks at her like she was handed a rock, then goes.

memory.fact: Priya obeyed because Nimue's voice was the kind you obeyed.
Priya was last seen alive, heading for the exit.

event: Eleven seconds later the sky comes down, without a sound.
Through the east window the city folds inward along seams that were not there before.

memory.fact: As the Tower rose, the city folded away along impossible seams.

event: Up through the seam rises the Tower, a dark fluted column scored with rings.

memory.fact: The Tower rose through the seam.
The Tower is a dark fluted column scored with horizontal ring-divisions, its floors.
The Tower's surface refuses to resolve into stone, metal or glass.

event: Nimue counts about a hundred rings and cannot be sure even of that.

memory.fact: The Tower is the kind of tall that broke counting.
Nimue's eye reached about 100 floors and could not be sure even of that.

event: The Tower's shadow falls the wrong way, toward the brightening east.

memory.fact: The Tower's long black shadow falls the wrong way, toward the brightening east.
The Tower's shadow reaches for the dawn as no honest shadow could.
The Tower is lit as if by something on the far side of the sky that no one else can see.

event: The shadow crosses St. Brigid's: the lights, the call bells and the coffee machine die.

memory.fact: Where the Tower's shadow first swept the city, electric power and machine-sound died.

event: Gravity tilts toward the Tower, and a low hum settles in her teeth and bones.

memory.fact: The Tower exerts a gravity that points toward the Tower rather than down.
The wrong-gravity tide is felt in the inner ear and pulls survivors downhill to the base.
A sustained sub-audible hum is felt in the teeth and the long bones of the arms.

event: The air smells of ozone, and of a city with its power off.

memory.fact: A thick ozone smell accompanies the Tower.

event: At 00:54:40 Nimue has her back to the wall by the crash cart, still counting.

memory.fact: Counting the room is the one part of Nimue the System could not switch off.

event: A child screams in room 218.
In 218, three patients lie dead; a boy of about nine with a cast sits up, alive.

memory.fact: Marcus is a boy of about nine with a cast on one arm.
Marcus was a patient in room 218, a four-bed bay, at St. Brigid's.
Marcus is ascended.
The three other patients in Marcus's bay were unascended and died.

event: The window is gone, a clean seam in the air, and something has come through it.
It is greyhound-sized, all joints and wet grey hide, a cluster of System light for a face.
It turns, slow, toward the loudest soft thing in the room: the boy.
A System box names it: Threshold Warden, a Tier 0 scout that hunts by sound, fragile and fast.

memory.fact: A Threshold Warden came through the vanished window, hunting Marcus by sound.

event: Nimue snags on fragile and sees the flaw: the light-cluster is its eyes.

memory.fact: Nimue's third reflex was the cold clean reach toward the System's readout: show me how you break.

event: She crosses the room and covers the boy's head with her body: through me first.

memory.fact: Nimue's first reflex was her body thrown across the child as a wall.

event: Her right hand tears the IV pole off its wheeled base.

memory.fact: In room 218 Nimue tore an IV pole free of its base.
That second reflex is the oldest, meanest part of Nimue, which intends to win.

event: As the warden launches, she drives the pole's point into its reading face.

memory.fact: Nimue drove the pole through a Threshold Warden's reading-face, killing it to protect Marcus.
Nimue's second reflex was the steel torn up and driven home.

event: The warden shrieks and dissolves around the pole; the boy cries into her scrubs.

memory.fact: Nimue saved Marcus from the warden.
Nimue saved Marcus from the warden.

event: The System: Floor Spawn neutralized; subject engaged a Tier 0 hostile prior to Ascension.

memory.fact: The System noted: subject engaged a Tier 0 hostile prior to Ascension.

event: Nimue understands the System is scoring her: every reflex is data toward her worth.

memory.fact: The System is an indifferent scorer, not malicious.
The System scores continuously; every reflex is data toward deciding a subject's worth.
Nimue understands she is a number being refined.

event: At 00:49:03 she crouches and asks the boy his name: Marcus.

memory.fact: Marcus sobbed into the front of Nimue's scrubs and gave her his name.

event: She sends Marcus to Priya in the south stairwell, and does not tell him it will be okay.

memory.fact: Nimue told Marcus not to stop for anyone who wasn't moving.
Nimue told Marcus not to stop for anyone who wasn't moving.

event: Marcus runs.

memory.fact: At Nimue's order Marcus ran for the south stairwell to find the nurse Priya and get out.
At Nimue's order Marcus ran for the south stairwell to find the nurse Priya and get out.
Marcus was last seen alive, leaving the hospital.

event: At 00:48:51 Nimue weighs the pole and turns toward the seam and the Tower.
She walks into the city: streets intact, traffic dead, everything leaning toward the Tower.

memory.fact: The city's streets, cars and traffic lights were intact but emptying.
Everything in the city leaned toward the Tower under the wrong-gravity tide.

event: The other 0.6% are on the streets too.

memory.fact: Only 0.6% of assessed lifeforms ascended.

event: A man slumped over a bus wheel thins away like fog off glass, leaving ozone.

memory.fact: The bodies thinned and cleared the way a breath fogs and clears on glass, leaving ozone.
A man over a bus wheel was cleared.

event: A dead woman on a bench comes apart; her oranges roll into the gutter.

memory.fact: A woman on a bench was cleared, and her oranges kept being real after she was not.

event: All over the city the System tidies the dead away, on schedule.

memory.fact: Over the hour the System progressively subtracted the dead.
The clearing was not violent; it was tidying, on schedule.
The System reclaimed the unascended like a machine reclaiming storage.
The cull was two processes: instant death at assessment, then the hour-long clearing.

event: A knot of survivors huddles round a parked car; System text blooms over their heads.

memory.fact: Those who chose each other and false comfort over moving toward the Tower were marked.
A knot of people huddling around a parked car was marked to be cleared when the count hit zero.

event: Nimue does not stop: engage, or be cleared.

memory.fact: The ascended learned the rule fast: engage, or be cleared.

event: She does not look back, and lets her survivor's guilt push her on.

memory.fact: Nimue files her survivor's guilt behind the engine and lets it push her onward.
Forward, toward the Tower, was the only verb the System left.

event: A dozen others converge on the Tower's base, none of them talking.

memory.fact: Nimue names her view of the city the dead city.
Each individual sees only their own interface.

event: Halfway there the System posts: one hundred floors stand between the ascended and the apex.

memory.fact: The Tower is a hundred-floor trial-structure.
The System states: One hundred floors stand between the ascended and the apex.

event: Each trial yields essence; her designation is HARVESTER. The Tower keeps what you cannot.

memory.fact: The System calls Nimue harvester.
Survivors of a trial gain essence.
The System says: Each is a trial. Each trial yields essence to those who survive it.

event: She sets harvester aside with everything she can't use yet, and keeps walking.
She recalls her mother: Nimue is a drowned-legend name, the lady who masters the tower.

memory.fact: Nimue's mother told her Nimue is an old story-name.
The Nimue of the story is a woman from a drowned legend.
That Nimue learned every word of a great wizard's magic.
That Nimue sealed the wizard in a tower of air, alone, forever.
Nimue's mother called the story-Nimue the lady who masters the tower.
Nimue's mother looked sad saying it; Nimue was six and didn't understand why.

event: She lets the legend go: work clears floors.
At the Tower's base the threshold is a seam in the world, edged in blue-white.

memory.fact: The seam is a vertical wound in the air taller than three people, edged in System blue-white.
The seam opens onto nothing: not darkness, but absence, a lightless held breath.

event: Others reach their own seams along the base, each alone; the clock reads 00:11:46.

memory.fact: The Tower's base presents a seam in the world, for each ascendant separately.

event: Nimue steps up to the line and sets down the pole's foot; the seam does not open.

memory.fact: The hum and the ozone intensify near the Tower's base.

event: The System asks for an anchor: when the System fell, what did you reach for?

memory.fact: The seam is the Ascension Threshold to Floor 1.
The Tower does not admit the empty.

event: Option A, Last Stand: her body made a wall for the child; +3 VIT.
Option B, Killing Edge: the pole torn loose and driven home; +2 PWR, +1 SPD.
Option C, Open Eye: the reach for the interface itself; +2 ATT, +1 INS.
Three versions of one instant in room 218 take shape in the blue-white air.

memory.fact: Three reflexes fired together in room 218, and they define Nimue.

event: Behind her the last of the unascended thin into ozone, and the dead city goes quiet.
Nimue stands on the line, and the seam waits to be told what to make of her.
